name: vehicle-traffic-routing-visual
description: Visual check: multiple vehicles on shared navmesh cause congestion with waiting state and traffic jam alert. Confirmed via direct engine trace (Finding #22) that the traffic_jam event genuinely fires at tick 35 (10 driver-boarding ticks added ahead of the move commands by #947, +25) once the tick budget was corrected — see the tick 26 step for detail.

steps.description: campaign start replaces the whole GameState (createGameForLevel), cash included, so `cash:` belongs here and nowhere earlier. $150,000 covers 4 drivers ($800 each) plus 4 tier-1 debris haulers ($25,000 each) = $103,200 — and all 4 haulers converging on one tile is precisely what makes this scenario's jam fire, so underfunding it would take the feature under test with it.

expect.note: the cash: override replaces dusty_hollow's $50,000 default outright

steps.description: Opens the Fleet panel and buys hauler #1 by clicking its tier-1 dealership row. The three buys below reuse the open panel.

Hauler #2, bought by clicking the same dealership row again: $121,800 in hand against $25,000. awaitUsable is the affordability assertion -- FleetPanel disables a tier row on cash < purchaseCost, so an underfunded run fails here instead of buying anyway.
Hauler #3, same row again: $96,800 in hand against $25,000.
Hauler #4, same row again: $71,800 in hand against $25,000. This is the vehicle that makes the jam reachable -- detectTrafficJam needs 3 vehicles waiting on a tile a 4th already occupies.

#947: canTickVehicle now requires a driver aboard to advance on tick at all, so each hauler needs its own driver boarded before the move commands below can succeed. The Fleet panel's own Assign/Unassign controls were removed in #921 -- `vehicle driver` survives as a scenario/console-only primitive, run as a bootstrap command rather than a UI click (same pattern as hauling-gate.json).

All four drivers spawn on the same tile as their haulers (#512), so 10 ticks is enough for every one of them to walk over and board -- confirmed live: `vehicle list` afterward shows driver:#1..#4 on all four. Shifts every absolute tick number the rest of this file's Finding #22 timing analysis depends on by +10 -- see the tick 6/tick 26 steps below.

Real click path for the one hauler a mouse can actually pick: select #1 in the 3D scene, rest the cursor on (37,33), press the selection bar's MOVE HERE. The old description here claimed no UI drives this command and none should exist -- false since the SelectionBar gained `move_here` (G4), usable with a mouse since ScenePicking started latching `.aim` (47f4fef). The focus point is the tile centre, measured in a real browser until the dispatched command read `vehicle move 1 to:37,33`. The three steps below stay console commands for a reason recorded there.

Fixed by issue #512: all four haulers spawn on ONE tile (vehicle buy stagger gets undone by NavGrid.findNearestReachableCell snapping every one of them to the same reachable cell), so scene-raycast clickEntity could only ever pick hauler #1 -- clickEntity for #2/#3/#4 always raycast onto #1 instead, with the selection bar reading "Debris Hauler #1" every time. FleetPanel rows are clickable now, so hauler #2 gets selected by clicking its Fleet panel row (`#bs-vehicle-panel [data-vehicle-id="2"]`), routed through ScenePicking.select(), then MOVE HERE drives the same `vehicle move` command as the hauler #1 step above.

Fixed by issue #512, same fix as hauler #2 above: hauler #3 gets selected via its Fleet panel row (`#bs-vehicle-panel [data-vehicle-id="3"]`) instead of the scene raycast that could only ever hit hauler #1.

Fixed by issue #512, same fix as haulers #2/#3 above: hauler #4 gets selected via its Fleet panel row (`#bs-vehicle-panel [data-vehicle-id="4"]`) instead of the scene raycast that could only ever hit hauler #1.

Split from a single tick 20 into smaller batches so a screenshot lands mid-route, before every vehicle has arrived and gone idle — TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_TICKS=10 needs at least that many ticks of contention, so the congestion shot is captured around cumulative tick 12, not tick 20+ (#411).

expect.note: all 4 vehicles still converging on (37,33) — real jam confirmed at tick 35 (shifted +10 by #947's driver-boarding ticks), see the tick 26 step below (Finding #22)

steps.description: Finding #22: a direct engine trace (sampling state.events.pendingEvent tick by tick) found the jam actually fires at absolute tick 25, not tick 20 as this step previously assumed — the previous 6+16=22 tick budget was 3 ticks short and left the event unfired every run. Extended to 6+26=32 for real margin past the confirmed tick-25 fire point (verified: all 4 vehicles converge on (37,33), vehicle #1 occupies it, #2/#3/#4 all enter the waiting state simultaneously and cross TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_TICKS=10 together, satisfying TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_VEHICLES=3 — unlike vehicle-traffic.json's Finding #21, converging all 4 purchased vehicles rather than 3 is exactly what makes this one work). #947 added 10 driver-boarding ticks ahead of the move commands, shifting every absolute tick number in this analysis by +10 — the jam now fires at tick 35, confirmed live: 16+26=42 tick budget still lands with the same margin past it.

expect.note: the step's own console output is the direct evidence: "[tick 35] EVENT: Traffic Jam ... (Advanced 19 of 26 requested ticks)" — the tick loop stops on the pending event, which is why tickCount lands on 35 rather than 42 (both shifted +10 from the pre-#947 25/32 by the driver-boarding ticks added ahead of the move commands). No scalar field exists in SerializableGameState to assert the event directly, so this anchors on the fleet staying intact at 4 while the jam condition is met.
